title: Connector SDK
what: Provide a versioned connector interface for discover, extract, checkpoint, health and replay.
why: New sources must not change graph-core logic.
behavior: Each connector emits SourceEvent records and owns source-specific auth/pagination only.
failure: Connector isolation; retryable failures checkpoint; poison records to DLQ.
test: Contract tests against a fake source.
done: A new connector can be added without editing ingestion core.

title: Jira JSON connector
what: Import configurable Jira JSON plus the synthetic MVP fixture.
why: Jira is the primary work-management seed for traceability.
behavior: Map source fields through configuration into canonical WorkItem/Project/Person entities.
failure: Malformed records rejected individually with evidence; run continues.
done: Repeat import is idempotent and creates expected graph.

title: Git repository connector
what: Inspect local Git repositories without network access.
why: The MVP must link work to commits and code.
behavior: Read refs, commits, authors, changed paths and commit messages using local git.
failure: Invalid repo/path traversal rejected; repository errors do not corrupt prior data.
done: Repository, branch and commit nodes plus modifications exist.

title: GitLab metadata adapter
what: Support GitLab-style MR/pipeline metadata from configurable API or local JSON fixture.
why: The E2E story includes merge requests and pipelines.
behavior: MVP supports fixture/offline mode; live on-prem GitLab adapter uses endpoint/token abstraction.
failure: Rate limits/retries/checkpoints; no hard-coded credential.
test: Mock API and fixture contract tests.
done: MR and pipeline records link to commits and work items.

title: Connector resiliency
what: Implement pagination, retry/backoff, rate-limit handling, checkpointing and resume.
why: Enterprise ingestion must survive partial failure.
behavior: Persist checkpoint atomically in local state volume after committed graph batch.
failure: Bounded retries then DLQ/failure state.
done: Restart resumes without duplicate canonical nodes.

title: Dry run and replay
what: Allow validation-only dry run and deterministic replay of captured source events.
why: Safe mapping evolution and debugging need reproducibility.
behavior: Dry run performs parse/map/validation without graph mutation; replay reads raw-capture events.
failure: Invalid replay schema/version is quarantined.
done: Same input/version produces same canonical mutations.

title: Source deletion semantics
what: Represent source disappearance/deletion without silent hard delete.
why: Historical provenance must not be destroyed.
behavior: Mark tombstone/deleted_at; hard delete is separate administrative operation.
failure: Conflicting source state becomes validation finding.
done: Deleted source is queryable historically and excluded from current views.

title: Confluence connector
what: Add on-prem Confluence connector through Connector SDK.
why: Documentation traceability requires enterprise wiki ingestion.
behavior: Deferred from MVP; support pages, spaces, attachments metadata and deltas.
failure: Same connector failure model.
done: Incremental sync and provenance pass.

title: ServiceNow connector
what: Add on-prem ServiceNow incident/problem/change/KB connector.
why: Operations traceability needs service-management data.
behavior: Deferred from MVP behind Connector SDK.
failure: Rate limits and schema drift isolated.
done: Incremental sync and mappings pass.

title: Raw capture
what: Persist immutable local SourceEvent envelopes before normalization.
why: Replay, provenance and audit require source fidelity.
behavior: Write newline-delimited JSON by source/run/date with hashes and restrictive permissions.
failure: Disk-full fails job before graph mutation of uncaptured record.
done: Every graph mutation references a captured event.

title: Canonicalization
what: Normalize source events into typed canonical entities/relationships.
why: Cross-source graph logic requires stable contracts.
behavior: Pure/config-driven mappers emit versioned NormalizedEntity/Relationship records.
failure: Mapper errors are per-record findings/DLQ.
done: Same source record maps deterministically for same mapper version.

title: Idempotent mutation
what: Use deterministic canonical IDs and mutation upserts.
why: Repeated sync must not duplicate graph facts.
behavior: Canonical IDs hash namespace/type/source identity; edges use deterministic semantic key.
failure: Conflict surfaces validation finding; no blind merge.
done: Second identical run does not increase logical entity/edge counts.

title: Ingestion job lifecycle
what: Track queued/running/succeeded/partial/failed/cancelled states.
why: Admin UI and recovery need truthful state.
behavior: Each run records counts, checkpoint, timings, versions and errors in meta graph and local logs.
failure: Worker crash leaves resumable state.
done: Admin UI reflects actual backend run state.

title: Dead-letter processing
what: Store rejected events locally with reason/evidence and replay controls.
why: Bad records must not block whole imports.
behavior: DLQ files contain event hash, stage, error code, safe message, run ID.
failure: Secrets/PII are not duplicated beyond allowed capture.
done: Rejected records are inspectable and replayable.

title: HugeGraph authoritative store
what: Use Apache HugeGraph as the authoritative property graph and ontology operational store.
why: This is a non-negotiable platform constraint.
behavior: All user-visible entity/relationship truth is resolved from HugeGraph; raw files are evidence, not alternative truth DB.
failure: Graph unavailable returns degraded/readiness failure; no shadow DB fallback.
done: All demo graph paths survive service restart.

title: Logical graph domains
what: Represent Jira, Code, Docs, CI, Provenance, Meta and other domains explicitly within the graph.
why: Avoid one undifferentiated graph while preserving native cross-domain traversal.
behavior: MVP uses one physical graph with graph_domain property and domain meta nodes; later physical isolation only by measured need.
failure: Unknown domain is rejected by schema policy.
done: Every business vertex/edge belongs to a valid domain.

title: Schema bootstrap
what: Initialize property keys, vertex labels, edge labels and indexes idempotently.
why: `docker compose up` must create a usable environment.
behavior: Schema bootstrap compares expected schema version before applying additive changes.
failure: Incompatible migration fails startup of app mutation path but preserves DB.
done: Fresh stack auto-initializes and second run is no-op.

title: Canonical identifiers
what: Define deterministic IDs independent of HugeGraph internal IDs where possible.
why: Traceability and replay cannot depend on unstable database identifiers.
behavior: canonical_id is the platform identity; source aliases map to it; ambiguous identities stay separate.
failure: Collision is a blocking validation error.
done: Every canonical entity has unique stable canonical_id.

title: Meta graph
what: Model datasets, sources, graph domains, schema/ontology versions, ingestion runs, quality and lineage metadata.
why: The query router and admin UI need graph self-description.
behavior: Meta nodes are queryable and link to domain data via INGESTED_IN/BELONGS_TO_DOMAIN/EVIDENCED_BY.
failure: Stale meta state is validation finding.
done: Admin statistics are derived from graph/meta records.

title: Cross-domain bridge edges
what: Create explicit, evidence-backed edges between work, code, CI and documents.
why: The value proposition is end-to-end enterprise traceability.
behavior: Link deterministic identifiers first (issue keys, commit SHA, paths); inferred links are labeled and scored.
failure: Low-confidence inference never becomes deterministic truth.
done: Jira→MR→Commit→File→Function→Dependency→Pipeline→Doc path is traversable.

title: Gremlin repository
what: Centralize parameterized/bounded Gremlin templates.
why: Unrestricted model-generated graph queries are unsafe.
behavior: Only named templates and validated QueryPlans reach the graph client in MVP.
failure: Unknown template or over-limit request rejected.
done: No UI/agent endpoint can execute arbitrary mutation Gremlin.

title: Index strategy
what: Create indexes only for measured access patterns.
why: Over-indexing increases write/storage cost.
behavior: MVP indexes canonical/source IDs, issue keys, commit SHA, qualified symbol name, path/domain/type and selected timestamps.
failure: Index bootstrap mismatch blocks incompatible mutation.
done: Benchmark-critical lookup paths use planned indexes.

title: Graph version journal
what: Record mutation run, schema/ontology version, first/last seen and validity metadata.
why: Reproducibility needs temporal/version context.
behavior: MVP stores revisions/change journal metadata; full snapshots/diffs are P5.
failure: Missing version metadata is validation error.
done: Each changed fact can be attributed to a run/version.

title: RDF/OWL interoperability
what: Export platform ontology/data through explicit adapters rather than claiming native RDF/SPARQL.
why: Interoperability is useful but HugeGraph is a property graph.
behavior: P2 export maps canonical vocabulary to RDF/OWL; SPARQL, if added, targets an adapter, not raw HugeGraph.
failure: Unsupported construct reports mapping loss.
done: No documentation claims native SPARQL support.

title: Enterprise ontology vocabulary
what: Version organization, work, code, CI/CD, operations, knowledge and AI/agent concepts.
why: Cross-source semantics require a controlled vocabulary.
behavior: Terms have URI/name, definition, domain/range, cardinality and lifecycle status.
failure: Unknown/deprecated term creates validation error/warning.
done: MVP entities/edges reference ontology version and valid terms.

title: Relationship semantics
what: Distinguish containment, identity, dependency, implementation, authorship, provenance, temporal and cross-domain semantics.
why: Generic RELATED_TO edges destroy explainability.
behavior: Every edge label has explicit domain/range, direction, inverse semantics where relevant and evidence policy.
failure: Invalid endpoints rejected or quarantined.
done: No MVP business relationship relies on untyped generic edge.

title: Evidence model
what: Attach source reference, event hash, extraction time, mapper/parser version, confidence and creation status.
why: Answers and inferred links must be defensible.
behavior: Evidence nodes/records link to entities and relationships; DETERMINISTIC/INFERRED/HUMAN_CONFIRMED status is mandatory.
failure: Missing evidence makes inferred fact invalid.
done: MVP evidence coverage is 100% for cross-domain bridge edges.

title: Provenance traversal
what: Support reverse traversal from graph fact to source event and ingestion run.
why: Audit/debugging needs chain of custody.
behavior: API exposes evidence references and lineage path.
failure: Missing source artifact is reported, not hidden.
done: User can trace demo answer to source fixture/commit metadata.

title: Deterministic identity resolution
what: Resolve exact emails, canonical source IDs and configured aliases before fuzzy methods.
why: Avoid accidental person/service merging.
behavior: Generate candidate set and auto-merge only deterministic rules.
failure: Conflict preserved as separate nodes.
done: Exact aliases merge predictably and retain source aliases.

title: Ambiguous identity candidates
what: Never silently merge low-confidence fuzzy matches.
why: False identity merges contaminate the enterprise graph.
behavior: Store candidate relationship/confidence for review; human-confirmed merge is future UI.
failure: Ambiguous candidates remain separate.
done: No fuzzy-only match produces same canonical_id automatically.

title: Bitemporal-ready fields
what: Store created/modified/deleted, first/last seen, valid_from/valid_to and source_version where available.
why: Enterprise topology changes over time.
behavior: MVP writes fields and current-state queries; historical reconstruction/diff is P5.
failure: Invalid intervals generate validation findings.
done: MVP schema is ready for P5 without ID rewrite.

title: Deterministic code parser
what: Parse source using Tree-sitter/language-specific AST tooling, never LLM as primary parser.
why: Code relationships must be reproducible.
behavior: Parser plugins emit File and CodeSymbol records with ranges, qualified names and structural relationships.
failure: Parse errors become file-level findings and do not abort repository.
done: Supported files yield stable symbol graph and exact source ranges.

title: Python and TypeScript MVP parsing
what: Support Python and TypeScript/JavaScript in Phase 1.
why: Two common languages prove parser extensibility without over-scoping.
behavior: Tree-sitter grammars/plugins extract modules/classes/functions/methods/imports/calls where statically resolvable.
failure: Unsupported syntax is partial with confidence/status.
done: Demo repo symbols and imports/calls are queryable.

title: Commit-to-symbol linking
what: Relate commits to files and affected symbols using changed ranges/versions where available.
why: Requirements must trace below file level.
behavior: MVP maps changed files deterministically and intersects diff hunks with symbol ranges when possible.
failure: Ambiguous deleted/renamed symbols produce evidence-backed partial link.
done: Demo commit connects to relevant function(s).

title: Call/import/dependency edges
what: Represent calls, imports and package/module dependencies with provenance.
why: Impact analysis needs dependency structure.
behavior: Static extractor emits typed edges and marks unresolved/external targets explicitly.
failure: Dynamic calls are not fabricated.
done: Blast radius traverses only validated edge classes.

title: Source navigation
what: Preserve repo, revision, path and line/column ranges.
why: VS Code must open exact context.
behavior: API returns workspace-relative path plus range and commit/revision evidence.
failure: Missing local checkout returns context without unsafe file access.
done: Extension opens demo symbol at correct range.

title: Structured QueryPlan
what: Represent user/agent query intent as a typed plan before Gremlin.
why: Separates interpretation from execution and enables policy.
behavior: QueryPlan contains intent, anchors, relationship allowlist, depth, filters, limits and evidence mode.
failure: Invalid/oversized plans rejected before graph call.
done: All NL and structured requests compile to validated QueryPlan.

title: Path query
what: Find bounded paths between known entities.
why: Core traceability questions are path questions.
behavior: Use template with max depth, relationship allowlist, timeout and result cap.
failure: No path returns empty evidence-backed result; timeout is explicit.
done: Demo Jira-to-function path returns expected ordered edges.

title: Impact analysis
what: Compute directional bounded blast radius using configured impact edge semantics.
why: Users need change consequences, not generic neighborhoods.
behavior: Traverse allowlisted dependency/call/implementation edges, dedupe, rank by path length/evidence and report why each node is included.
failure: Cycles bounded; partial results marked on timeout.
test: Cyclic graph and golden blast-radius tests.
done: Demo function change returns expected dependents with paths.

title: Entity search
what: Search by canonical/source IDs, issue key, commit SHA, symbol/path and names.
why: Users need reliable anchors before traversal.
behavior: Exact/indexed identifiers first; bounded text/name match second.
failure: Broad queries require minimum term and result cap.
done: Demo Jira issue, commit and symbol are discoverable.

title: Natural-language query interpretation
what: Interpret supported NL intents locally and safely.
why: Natural interaction improves usability without sacrificing graph safety.
behavior: Rule/regex fast path handles canonical questions; local LLM may produce QueryPlan JSON only, never executable Gremlin.
failure: Model failure falls back to deterministic intents or requests structured refinement.
done: Prompt injection cannot bypass QueryPlan policy.

title: Query safety policy
what: Enforce traversal depth, result count, timeout, relationship/property allowlists and read-only mode.
why: Graph queries can be computationally expensive or destructive.
behavior: Policy validates plans and server-side execution wrapper cancels/limits work where supported.
failure: Violation returns stable error code and audit event.
done: All exposed query endpoints pass policy conformance suite.

title: Query evidence envelope
what: Every derived result can include paths, fact IDs and evidence references.
why: Explainability requires more than answer text.
behavior: API returns answer-independent GraphResult/Evidence objects.
failure: Missing evidence is visible in result quality.
done: GraphRAG/UI/MCP consume same evidence format.

title: Raw Gremlin admin boundary
what: Do not expose unrestricted Gremlin to user app, agent or MCP.
why: Prevents arbitrary traversal/mutation and injection.
behavior: Developer-only local diagnostic path is disabled by default and never used by normal flows.
failure: Disabled path returns 404/403-like policy response.
done: No public OpenAPI/MCP tool accepts free-form Gremlin in MVP.

title: Graph validation rules
what: Execute rule packs for orphan, endpoint/domain-range, duplicate, provenance, mandatory edge, type and dangling reference checks.
why: Graph correctness must be measurable.
behavior: Rules produce ValidationFinding with rule, severity, entity/edge refs, evidence and remediation.
failure: Rule failure isolated and reported.
done: Admin UI shows real findings from demo data.

title: Validation gates
what: Block or quarantine mutations that violate hard invariants; soft rules run post-ingestion.
why: Not all quality defects have equal risk.
behavior: ERROR invariants prevent commit; WARN/INFO findings persist.
failure: Partial batches are rolled back or safely marked by mutation strategy.
done: Invalid endpoint edge cannot silently enter graph.

title: Graph quality metrics
what: Compute completeness, freshness, orphan rate, duplicate rate, provenance/evidence coverage and schema compliance.
why: Admin users need trendable graph health.
behavior: Metrics derive from validation and graph stats; MVP computes per run/domain.
failure: Unknown denominator reported as N/A, not false zero/100%.
done: Dashboard values reconcile with fixture counts.

title: Retrieval router
what: Choose direct graph, linked documents, code context, graph+text hybrid or no retrieval.
why: Avoid unnecessary LLM/vector infrastructure and token use.
behavior: Deterministic intent rules first; pluggable local classifier later.
failure: Unknown intent chooses conservative graph/search path.
done: Known MVP questions route without external service.

title: GraphRAG evidence retrieval
what: Retrieve entities, relationships, paths, neighborhoods, provenance and linked documents.
why: Answers must be grounded in authoritative graph context.
behavior: Convert bounded GraphResult into context blocks with stable citations.
failure: Insufficient evidence yields explicit insufficiency, not invention.
done: Demo GraphRAG answer cites graph/source references.

title: Local model abstraction
what: Provide model interface for chat/generation and optional embeddings with all external providers disabled in MVP.
why: Local-first is non-negotiable and future providers must not leak enterprise data.
behavior: Configuration supports a local OpenAI-compatible/Ollama-style adapter; external adapter code is disabled by policy.
failure: Model-down degrades to graph results and deterministic summaries.
done: Core search/path/impact remains usable with model service stopped.

title: No mandatory vector DB in MVP
what: Do not require a second database for semantic retrieval in Phase 1.
why: Infrastructure must stay minimal.
behavior: Use graph, metadata, document sections and local lexical retrieval; optional embeddings may be evaluated in-process/file-indexed.
failure: Semantic-only request reports reduced capability if embeddings disabled.
done: MVP starts and demos without vector database.

title: RAG evaluation harness
what: Measure retrieval precision/recall, context relevance, evidence coverage, groundedness, answer correctness, latency and token usage.
why: RAG quality must be testable.
behavior: Golden QA dataset includes expected entities/paths/evidence.
failure: Failed generation does not erase retrieval metrics.
done: Baseline report is reproducible locally.

title: Adaptive RAG strategy framework
what: Expose strategy interface for simple/graph/hybrid/corrective/self/adaptive/agentic/multi-hop variants without instantiating all.
why: Future expansion should not rewrite retrieval.
behavior: Strategy selected by router and capability/config; Phase 3 adds advanced variants based on evaluation.
failure: Unsupported strategy rejected cleanly.
done: P3 can add strategy plugin without changing callers.

title: Agent contract
what: Define ID/type/purpose/input/output/capabilities/tools/model/memory/policies/time/budget/retry/failure/evidence/audit fields.
why: Agents require enforceable runtime contracts.
behavior: Registry loads versioned YAML/JSON definitions and validates before execution.
failure: Invalid contract cannot register.
done: Every enabled agent has a validated contract.

title: Bounded agent runtime
what: Enforce maximum steps/retries/recursion/time/model/tool budgets and circuit breaker.
why: Prevents unbounded loops and resource use.
behavior: Runtime state machine records route/context/plan/tool/observation/evaluation/result/audit.
failure: Budget exhaustion terminates with partial evidence.
done: Agent cannot exceed configured execution envelope.

title: TraceImpact agent
what: Provide one useful read-only MVP workflow that answers requirement/code trace and impact questions.
why: MVP requires a real agent without unsafe write autonomy.
behavior: Agent composes search/path/impact/retrieval tools and returns evidence summary.
failure: Tool/model failures are surfaced with partial structured result.
done: Same demo question works via UI/API/MCP context.

title: Write/action approval boundary
what: Separate read tools from write/destructive tools and require explicit confirmation for future write actions.
why: Agent autonomy must not bypass human control.
behavior: MVP registers read tools only; future action registry includes risk/reversibility/approval policy.
failure: Unapproved write invocation denied/audited.
done: No MVP agent can mutate source systems or code.

title: Controlled self-modification
what: Self-learning/evolving/writing capabilities remain disabled until governance, sandboxing, tests and approval exist.
why: Autonomous self-change is high risk.
behavior: Architecture reserves versioned proposal/sandbox interfaces only; implementation is P8+.
failure: Any runtime self-edit request denied in earlier phases.
done: No production self-modification path exists before P8+.

title: Scoped memory records
what: Model working/task/conversation/semantic/episodic/procedural memory with scope/source/TTL/provenance/confidence/classification/deletion policy.
why: Agent memory must be governable.
behavior: MVP persists only task/audit evidence needed for TraceImpact; broad long-term memory is later.
failure: Expired/forbidden memory excluded.
done: No uncontrolled accumulation in MVP.

title: MCP read server
what: Expose search_entity/get_entity/neighbors/path/query/impact/code/jira/document/lineage/evidence as local MCP tools/resources.
why: Developer and agent clients need standard context access.
behavior: Thin adapter calls same application services and policy layer as REST.
failure: Backend/policy errors map to structured MCP errors.
done: MCP returns same graph evidence as REST for demo case.

title: MCP action separation
what: Keep write/action tools in separate registry and disabled in MVP.
why: Protocol access must not expand authority.
behavior: Action tools require explicit config, risk policy and confirmation in later phases.
failure: Disabled writes are not advertised.
done: MVP MCP surface is read-only.

title: User web application
what: Provide search/NL query, graph visualization, details/evidence, path and impact views backed by real APIs.
why: MVP must demonstrate value interactively.
behavior: React/TypeScript app uses /api/v1; no hardcoded domain responses.
failure: API failure shows explicit degraded/error state.
done: Demo flow works from persisted data.

title: Graph explorer
what: Visualize typed nodes/edges with filters, expansion, path highlighting and provenance.
why: Users need interpretable graph navigation.
behavior: Cytoscape.js loaded locally; server returns bounded subgraphs.
failure: Large result prompts/refuses expansion beyond cap.
done: Demo path is highlighted with evidence access.

title: Admin ingestion UI
what: Show connectors, runs, status, counts, errors, replay/dry-run controls.
why: Operations must reflect real system state.
behavior: Admin routes call ingestion APIs; URL separation is not authorization.
failure: Actions validate local auth/confirmation.
done: Run state reconciles with backend/meta graph.

title: Admin graph quality UI
what: Show graph stats, validation findings, quality metrics, schema/ontology versions and backup state.
why: Demonstrates maintainability and trust.
behavior: All values queried from APIs/meta graph.
failure: Missing metric displayed as unavailable.
done: No dashboard KPI is hardcoded.

title: VS Code context extension
what: Provide sidebar/webview showing current file/symbol, Jira, commits, dependencies, docs and provenance.
why: Developer workflow is a required product surface.
behavior: Extension resolves local workspace path/symbol and calls platform API over configured local endpoint.
failure: Unavailable platform shows offline state; no source modification.
done: Opening demo function retrieves correct graph context.

title: VS Code trace/impact commands
what: Commands answer why code exists and what change may affect.
why: Makes enterprise graph actionable in editor.
behavior: Commands invoke path/impact services and render evidence.
failure: No unrestricted Gremlin/tool execution.
done: Demo command returns Jira→code path and impact.

title: No outbound enterprise-data egress
what: Disable external LLM/API egress by default and document firewall/Docker network controls.
why: Enterprise data must remain local.
behavior: MVP services need no internet at runtime after images/models are staged.
failure: Blocked egress fails closed; audit safe error.
done: Demo succeeds with external network disabled.

title: Secret isolation
what: Credentials are never hardcoded/logged and use mounted secret files/env references.
why: Connector/model/admin secrets require protection.
behavior: Secret loader resolves file references; redaction filter protects logs.
failure: Missing secret fails connector without exposing value.
done: Repository and logs contain no test secret plaintext.

title: Input/file safety
what: Validate paths, sizes, MIME/extension expectations, archive behavior and URL endpoints.
why: Ingestion handles untrusted enterprise artifacts.
behavior: Restrict to configured roots; reject traversal/symlink escape; bound files and parsers.
failure: Unsafe input quarantined.
done: Security suite rejects malicious fixtures.

title: Prompt/tool injection defenses
what: Treat retrieved content as data, not instructions, and validate all tool plans.
why: Malicious docs/code can manipulate agents.
behavior: Context delimiters, instruction hierarchy, tool allowlists, QueryPlan schema/policy and output validation.
failure: Injection attempt cannot add tool or exceed query policy.
done: Known injection cases remain read-only/bounded.

title: Authentication without MVP RBAC
what: Protect non-loopback deployments with single-user/local authentication while not implementing role matrices.
why: No RBAC does not mean unauthenticated exposure.
behavior: Loopback dev may use dev token; controlled demo uses configured local credential and CSRF-safe patterns.
failure: Missing auth in non-dev profile blocks startup/exposure.
done: /admin route presence is never claimed as authorization boundary.

title: Container hardening
what: Use non-root where practical, read-only FS where practical, dropped capabilities, healthchecks and private networks.
why: Reduces local attack surface.
behavior: Compose separates public app edge from internal graph/model networks.
failure: Hardening exception documented.
done: HugeGraph/model not exposed externally by default.

title: Audit events
what: Record auth, ingestion, query, agent/tool, admin mutation, backup/restore and policy-denial events.
why: Operational accountability is required.
behavior: Structured append-only local audit stream plus selected graph meta references; never private chain-of-thought.
failure: Audit write failure blocks high-risk action and alerts; read query may degrade per policy.
done: Sensitive operation has traceable audit ID.

title: Restart-safe processing
what: Workers recover from crash using checkpoints and idempotent graph mutations.
why: Local containers will restart.
behavior: Run state persists to mounted state volume/meta graph.
failure: Unclean shutdown detected and resumed/reconciled.
done: No duplicates or silent skipped records after restart.

title: Backup and restore
what: Provide repeatable graph schema+data backup and restore plus config/raw-state backup guidance.
why: MVP acceptance explicitly requires recovery.
behavior: Use HugeGraph-supported tooling for graph export/restore and checksummed archive; run scripted verification query.
failure: Failed backup never marked successful; restore uses clean target/test mode.
done: Restored demo reproduces expected counts/path queries.

title: Structured logging and health
what: Expose structured logs, liveness/readiness and correlation IDs locally.
why: Troubleshooting must not depend on cloud observability.
behavior: JSON logs to stdout/file, /health/live, /health/ready; correlation spans ingestion/query/agent.
failure: Dependency failure makes readiness false.
done: Failure can be followed by correlation ID.

title: Local metrics
what: Expose Prometheus-format metrics for ingestion, graph queries, RAG/model, agents, tools and errors.
why: Performance/quality claims require measurement.
behavior: App /metrics; Prometheus/Grafana optional profile, not mandatory core.
failure: Metrics failure does not break core request path.
done: Key MVP metrics are machine-readable.

title: Benchmark-defined objectives
what: Define and run a representative local benchmark before claiming throughput/latency.
why: Arbitrary performance claims are prohibited.
behavior: Baseline dataset and hardware profile are versioned; report p50/p95/p99 and resource use.
failure: Missed targets create tuning issue, not hidden result.
test: Automated benchmark smoke + manual full run.
done: Published numbers identify dataset/hardware/version.

title: Modular monolith boundary
what: Use modular monolith services in Phase 1; split only on evidence.
why: Avoid premature distributed complexity.
behavior: Domain packages expose typed ports; API/worker/MCP reuse application services.
failure: Cross-module direct DB access rejected by architecture tests/convention.
done: Core can later split without changing external contracts.

title: Data minimization and classification
what: Capture only required source fields and classify sensitive content.
why: Local operation still requires privacy discipline.
behavior: Connector mappings define allow/deny/redaction; logs never copy document bodies by default.
failure: Unknown sensitive field defaults to protected handling.
done: Audit/log exports contain no prohibited content.
